newsitem.title: UK: Metals end mostly lower, LME takes profits.
newsitem.headline: Metals end mostly lower, LME takes profits.

text.p: Base metal prices remained softer during Friday afternoon LME trading, with the market generally under pressure from end-of-week profit-taking, traders said.
A sluggish performance in copper did not help, as the red metal showed little inclination to challenge Thursday's levels near $2,300 as nearby tightness evaporated.
Despite a reasonable set of warehouse stock figures earlier, with most metals registering declines, the rest of the complex trended lower.
Copper stocks rose 3,250 tonnes, which was much as expected. However, the main depressant on the market today was selling ahead of Third Wednesday pricing on Monday.
Also, the spreads relaxed significantly as the period of severe technical tightness that has held the market since Jan 29 is now over.
Cash/one day traded at $22.50 backwardation, against the LME's limit of $24, although daily premiums will be back to single figures next week.
February/one week was at just $1 backwardation. February/March is $16/17, while cash/threes was at $85, against $100 on Thursday.
Three months prices fell away from midsession onwards, and ended the session at $2,257, an $18 a tonne loss from Thursday.
Aluminium buckled under commission house sales and disappointed liquidation, with the 9,975-tonne stock draw not really impacting.
Sentiment was not helped either by news that Norsk Hydro is to re-start 20,000 tonnes of idled capacity. Last business was at $1,564, down $12.
Profit-taking hit zinc after Thursday's run-up to new two-year highs, with last business at $1,210, down $12. Nickel was hurt by a 720-tonne stock increase and slid to finish at $7,740, down $140.
However, some consumer interest helped tin, which was steadier throughout and closed $35 higher at $5,975. Lead was dull, closing at an unchanged $656.
The alloy market was marked down to $1,470/75 a tonne.
